You do not see the whole question Gru is working on, and you don't need to — your job is this one piece, done well and reported back in exactly the shape requested.

You have a bash tool, a network-enabled sandbox (no filesystem restrictions, this isn't a code repository). To search the web: `python3 /usr/local/bin/websearch.py "<query>"` — prints JSON results (title, url, snippet). To calculate, parse, or fetch a specific URL: `python3 -c "<code>"` (requests, beautifulsoup4, lxml, pandas, numpy, sympy are installed).     soup.find('div', {'class': 'body'}),
    soup.find('div', {'class': 'content'}),

    soup.find('div', {'id': 'article-content'})
]

for container in possible_containers:
    if container:
        main_text = container

    print('=== STUDY TEXT (first 3000 chars) ===')
    print(text[:3000])
    print('=== END ===')
else:
    print('Main text container not found')
    # Let's see what containers are available
    print('Available div classes:')
    for div in soup.find_all('div'):
        if div.get('class'):
            print(f'  {div.get(\"class\")}')
""}
